question: Compare the three meanings of 'index' in data wrangling.
answer: The term 'index' in data wrangling has three distinct meanings: [S1] 1. In a database context, it's a data structure for speeding up column lookups, as mentioned in [S1]. 2. In pandas, an Index holds the row labels of a DataFrame, as described in [S1]. 3. In Python, an index is an integer position starting at 0, as explained in [S1]. These are unrelated uses, [S1]

citations.title: Data Wrangling Handbook
citations.text:
5. Three Kinds of Index
A database index is a data structure that speeds up lookups on a column but makes writes slower
and uses extra storage. A pandas Index holds the row labels of a DataFrame. A Python list index is
an integer position starting at 0. These three meanings of the word index are unrelated.

S4.title: Data Glossary
S4.text:
NULL: the SQL marker for a missing value.
NaN: floating-point not-a-number used by pandas for missing numeric data.
None: Python's null object; pandas also treats None as missing in object columns.
key: the column or columns used to match rows when joining two tables.
schema: the names and data types of the columns of a table.
sample: DataFrame.sample(n=3) returns 3 random rows. It is a row draw, not a statistical sample design.
merge versus join: pd.merge joins on columns by default, whereas DataFrame.join joins on the index by default.
index: depends on context - database index, pandas Index or list position.
